newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean political parties agree on new labour law.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean political parties agree on new labour law.

text.p: South Korea's ruling and opposition parties agreed on Saturday on a new labour law to replace a bill that sparked almost four weeks of strikes after it was rammed through parliament last December, a parliamentary official said.
The new bill would be submitted to the National Assembly for a vote on March 10. the official said.

It delays implementation for two years of a clause in the original bill making it easier for companies to lay off workers, a provision that led to worker fury. However, it upholds the principle of "no work no pay" for striking workers, a key demand of employers.
In a concession to labour unions, it allows multiple trade union organisations at a national level, breaking the monopoly of the Korean Federation of Trade Unions.
President Kim Young-sam was forced to send the original bill back to parliament after its forced passage with no debate unleashed some of the worst industrial unrest in South Korean history.
